title: Work IQ: Listen lets agents subscribe to workplace events
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly treats tenant policy coverage of subscription creation as undocumented, although Listen creates subscriptions through an MCP creation tool and Microsoft documents policy evaluation for each tool request. The roadmap facts, preview behaviour, billing model and printed control paths and Graph operation are otherwise supported.

claims.where: Governance controls: mutation caveat; Open questions: create_entity
claims.claim: Whether the policy's default mutation restriction covers creating a Listen subscription is not stated.
claims.quote: A separate tenant policy layer evaluates each tool request and blocks mutation operations by default. Administrators can enable supported create, update, delete, and action requests through tenant policy.
claims.fix: Replace the mutation caveat with: 'Listen creates subscriptions with create_entity. Work IQ MCP tenant policy evaluates each tool request and blocks mutation operations by default; administrators can enable supported creation requests through tenant policy. Exact policy behaviour can depend on tenant configuration.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/tool-reference alongside the existing Listen and policy pages, and remove the corresponding Open questions bullet. This states the documented general reach without inventing a Listen-specific exception or guaranteed tenant outcome.

claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "licensing" "Tool API" credits rate. Read billing overview and spendingPolicy update in full: no Work IQ limit enforcement rule. Search excerpts from Plan licensing and cost additionally state that retries do not resolve exhausted spending limits.
claims.fix: Replace 'Whether a limit ends Work IQ API use is not read on these pages, so do not assume a limit stops it' with 'A spending policy defines limits, not a reserved credit allocation; repeated retries will not resolve an exhausted spending limit.'
